fields.Front: What should you always start with when building a database system: the data or the code?
fields.Back: The data, not the code. Build a model (ER diagram) before creating the database.

fields.Front: List the steps for figuring out what data to store (requirements for a large system).
fields.Back: Gather all reports the customers use/print/generate; look at screens where they enter/modify data; find the customers'/stakeholders' requirements; figure out how they view the data; integrate the views to get the minimal data to store.

fields.Text: The ER model was created by {{c1::Peter Chen}} in {{c2::1976}}.
Tools for drawing ER diagrams include {{c1::Microsoft Visio}}, {{c2::draw.io}} and {{c3::SmartDraw}}.

fields.Front: What blueprint examples does the instructor show to argue for modelling first?
fields.Back: The Wright brothers' original plane, a building blueprint with measurements and a visualization, and a baby gate.

fields.Text: Model first because otherwise you 'build something large and waste all your time... then you make a {{c1::mistake}}'; a model gets rid of {{c2::errors}} before building.
'From this day forward, I want you to think about your {{c1::data}} before you ever think how you're going to {{c2::code}} something.'

fields.Front: What hospital report and screen does the instructor use to show how to discover data to store?
fields.Back: A 'number of falls' report, and a patient-entry screen with first/middle/last name, date of death, laboratory details and SSN; each field reveals something that must be stored.

fields.Front: Why integrate the users' overlapping views of the data?
fields.Back: So each piece of data is stored once rather than twice for two different users; the code that accesses it gets it from that one spot.

fields.Front: Give two reasons the instructor gives for why an ER diagram is useful.
fields.Back: It can be read without knowing any code, so you can sit down with users and they will understand it; it is independent of any DBMS and is then mapped to the relational model (most common) or another model.

fields.Front: Visio, draw.io, SmartDraw: which is free for Western students, which is online, which needs a sign-up?
fields.Back: Visio is probably free for Western students; draw.io is online and free; SmartDraw requires signing up.

fields.Front: What advantage of Visio over draw.io does the instructor mention in Lesson 6?
fields.Back: Visio can help convert your ER diagram into a relational database; draw.io does not.
